packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-06: unverified blind image reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context proposed an identification or a reading for this packet. I read only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-004. I also ran one directory listing of the packet folder, which showed that packet.json exists. I did not open packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 and image-003 are overviews of the same inside board of a binding. image-003 is in the board's natural upright orientation. image-001 is the same board rotated 90 degrees so that the written strips read horizontally.
- The board has a limp parchment or leather turn-in around its edges and a central textile pastedown with a woven, moire-like pattern. At the spine edge, three sewing supports (twisted cords) come through, and parchment strips (spine linings or guards) sit between and beyond them. There are four strips in all.
- Two strips carry visible writing:
  (a) the strip between the 1st and 2nd cords counted from the head in image-003 (the 3rd strip from the left in image-001): Latin in a gothic cursive or bastarda hand, 5 lines visible. Native tile: image-002.
  (b) the strip at the tail, below the 3rd cord (lower right in image-003, leftmost in image-001): a vernacular, apparently German, text in a similar hand, 5 lines visible. Native tile: image-004.
- The other two strips (at the head, and between the 2nd and 3rd cords) show no legible ink in these images. They may be blank, or written on the hidden side.
- On both written strips, the text is cut off at the edge nearest the spine and partly covered or stained at the bottom. I see no rubrics, enlarged initials, glosses or columns. Each fragment is too small to show the page layout.
- The bottom line of strip (a) is under a dark stain and partly under the textile edge.

TRANSCRIPTION
Expansions are in parentheses. "?" follows an uncertain reading. [illegible] marks unreadable text. ' marks a visible abbreviation stroke or superscript that I have not expanded with confidence.

Strip (a), Latin. image-002, lines counted from the top of the strip. image-001 and image-003 show the same lines at lower resolution; they are not additional text.
image-002 l.1: De silencio dicit
image-002 l.2: vir sanctus in re^a   [the "re" has a superscript a: re(gul)a? The tail of "vir" is formed like z]
image-002 l.3: Faciam(us)? q(uo)d ait p(ro)ph(eta)   [first letter a large cursive F or S; the -us ending is a 9-shaped sign; p(ro)ph has a stroke crossing the descender and an h with a looped flourish]
image-002 l.4: D[i]xi? c(us)? [illegible: 1-2 letters, stained] stodi[a]m? vias   [the middle of the line is under a dark stain; "custodiam" is a tentative reading of the letter shapes: a long s, then "todi", then a minim group with a suspension stroke]
image-002 l.5: [illegible] ...ens? [illegible] ...e? lingu(a)?   [heavily stained and partly covered. Only the final word group, with suspension marks over two letters, is partly visible: lingu?/ung?]

Strip (b), vernacular (apparently German). image-004, lines counted from the top. Every line is cut off at the right edge.
image-004 l.1: Item fre[?]n[?]...   [a looped stroke before the I; then "fre" and a minim group, possibly "frem"/"freun", cut off]
image-004 l.2: Das m[?]n? k...   [possibly "Das man k", cut off]
image-004 l.3: vnd das er da...
image-004 l.4: vnd darumb? ...   [the last letters run into the edge]
image-004 l.5: wand'? sch[e]? o?f? ...   [the first word has a superscript abbreviation stroke after d; the second word may be "schz"/"sche"; the line is very uncertain and largely cut off]

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
- I attempted every visible written line on both strips: 5 lines each. Each strip shows no more text than that.
- Unread: the text cut off at the spine edge of both strips; the hidden side of all four strips; and anything under the textile pastedown. If the other side of the head strip or the middle strip carries writing, it is not visible here.

LIMITATIONS
- These are small binding strips (spine linings or guards), so most lines are truncated.
- Strip (a), lines 4-5: staining.
- Strip (b): the right edge is cut off, and some letterforms are ambiguous.
- No wider view of these strips exists in the packet. Images taken with the linings lifted, or raking-light images of the uninscribed strips, would be needed to read more.

Images I could not see: none. All four loaded.
